children: The new compact sedan is expected to get updated styling, petrol and CNG options and an electric version

Tata Motors is set to introduce its updated compact sedan as the Tata Aeris on 25 September. The new model is expected to take over from the Tigor nameplate, with Tata Motors giving the sedan a new identity along with changes to its exterior, cabin and powertrain options. The launch date has also been confirmed by Tata Motors through its teaser campaign.

The Aeris is expected to get a revised front-end with slimmer headlights, a black connecting element and a redesigned bumper. The rear could also receive new tail-lights, a new bumper and redesigned alloy wheels, although the basic sedan shape is expected to remain similar to the current Tigor.

Inside, the sedan could get a larger 10.25-inch touchscreen with wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay. Other expected features include a digital driver display, a new steering wheel, a 360-degree camera, wireless charging, Type-C ports and electrically folding outside rear-view mirrors.
Six airbags are also expected to be offered as part of the safety package.
The Tata Aeris is expected to be offered with petrol and CNG powertrains, while an electric version called the Aeris.ev is also expected to follow.

The petrol version could use a 1.2-litre engine producing 86 PS and 113 Nm of torque. The CNG version is expected to produce 75.5 PS and 96.5 Nm. Both versions could be offered with five-speed manual and automatic transmission options.
Tata Motors has not yet revealed the specifications of the Aeris. These details are expected to be announced at the 25 September launch.

The sedan will enter a segment that includes the Maruti Suzuki Dzire, Hyundai Aura and Honda Amaze. The Aeris name is expected to replace the Tigor as Tata Motors looks to give its compact sedan a fresh identity ahead of the festive season.
